source.title: TEVI: Text-Conditioned Editing of Visual Representations via Sparse Autoencoders for Improved Vision-Language Alignment
source.authors: S. Mahajan; Sukrut Rao; Jiahao Xie; Alexander Koller; B. Schiele

record.tranche_reason: Tests the semantic relevance and functional importance of SAE latents in CLIP visual embeddings, while reporting that meaningfulness is limited and that a mask without SAE disentanglement can perform comparably. It does not test superposition geometry or LLM representations.
record.gate_note: The natural-image SAE mask analysis and latent ablations bear on whether SAE dictionary features act as meaningful representation units. The controlled CG-SAE experiments assign predefined meanings to decoder weights, so they do not establish that unconstrained SAE dictionaries are canonical. Retrieval gains, alignment scores, and other TEVI results are not rows unless they directly measure latent meaning or latent ablation. No AI-directed instructions appear in the text.
record.test_reason: TEVI uses a TopK SAE over CLIP image embeddings as a tool for text-conditioned editing. Its results measure the learned mask and downstream retrieval, not whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units (V5). Nor do they test superposition geometry, capacity, polysemanticity or LLM features. The mask analysis (ρ>0.1 fraction, latent ablations) checks whether the mask is meaningful and selective. Its ablated quantity is TEVI's own retrieval (baseline 24.20 is TEVI, not base CLIP at 20.38). The CG-SAE experiments impose decoder meanings by construction.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that decomposing CLIP image embeddings into SAE concepts makes the information imbalance controllable. They report that TEVI preserves caption-described content, masks meaningfully and selectively, and improves retrieval. In the limitations, they note dependence on SAE accuracy and benchmark gains comparable to a no-SAE mask.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TopK SAEs over CLIP visual embeddings and a learned text-conditioned latent mask; it does not implement the Toy Models of Superposition method or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that mask behavior and retrieval depend on the conditioning caption; fine-grained datasets retain more latents than coarse-grained datasets. Negative-caption conditioning is necessary for the natural-image training setup, though that ablation is not a result about dictionary-feature canonicality.

fits_no_version.finding: On DOCCI, a mask over SAE latents selects the named object 79.4% of the time vs 55.6% for a mask on raw CLIP embeddings. A mask on a random SAE gives lower retrieval than TEVI (e.g. DOCCI I→T R@1 21.30 vs 24.20). However, retrieval gains are comparable to the no-SAE mask.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents of CLIP image embeddings support more concept-selective editing than raw embedding dimensions, without consistently better downstream retrieval.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Evidence is from CLIP-family visual embeddings, not LLM activations. The study does not test dictionary completeness, cross-seed or cross-model stability, or canonicality; concept identity is proxied by embedding similarity. The paper itself notes SAE accuracy limitations and comparable performance from a no-SAE mask in some retrieval settings.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the controlled CG-SAE classification and latent-specificity results because the decoder meanings were assigned from predefined synthetic concepts, rather than discovered by an unconstrained SAE; these do not establish canonicality of ordinary SAE features. Omitted general retrieval and alignment benchmark results because they measure TEVI performance rather than the claimed status of SAE features.

untested.parts: No toy models, feature-vs-dimension counts, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of neuron capacity competition.
No analysis of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
No LLMs; SAEs on CLIP vision embeddings are used as a tool, and recovery of sparse features is not assessed as evidence.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds/sizes, or canonicality of SAE features.
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Random-SAE masking ablation compared with TEVI and fine-tuned CLIP retrieval

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper (EMNLP) using SAEs as an editing tool on CLIP-family vision encoders. The reader's V5 linkage over-reads mask analyses as evidence about SAE features' status. No version of the superposition claim is tested, so no verdict labels are given.

versions.untested_parts: No test of feature count relative to dimensions, overlap, orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of neurons competing for capacity or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The study analyzes CLIP-family vision encoders, not LLMs, and does not measure features spread across neurons in LLMs.
Tests semantic association and functional relevance of some SAE latents in CLIP image embeddings, but not feature completeness, stability across training or models, or canonicality.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of active SAE latents whose mask value correlated with the caption-concept similarity at ρ > 0.1.
rows.note: The authors say not all latents are likely to be equally important; the concept proxy is cosine similarity between caption embeddings and SAE decoder dictionary vectors.
rows.check: Measures whether TEVI's learned mask correlates with caption-concept similarity. This evaluates the method's mask, not the canonicality, completeness or stability of SAE features.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Measured the same latent-mask correlation using a caption-shuffled null baseline.
rows.note: Null comparison for the reported 20% result.
rows.check: Null control for the mask-correlation analysis; same issue as r1.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Conditioned image embeddings on each of two named objects and measured whether the embedding was closer to its own conditioned object.
rows.note: Shows selective use of some SAE latents for a visual concept task, not completeness or canonicality of the dictionary.
rows.check: Selectivity of TEVI conditioning (79.4% vs 50% chance) is the study's own method performance, not a measure of SAE features as model units.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Applied the no-SAE mask baseline to the same named-object selection test.
rows.note: Compared with TEVI, the baseline is less selective but exceeds chance.
rows.check: No-SAE baseline compared with the study's method (55.6%); a method comparison, not a test of V5.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the top 32 SAE mask latents ranked by mask value and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.note: Ablating highly ranked latents substantially reduces retrieval, indicating functional relevance for this task.
rows.check: Ablates TEVI mask latents. The baseline 24.20 is TEVI's own R@1 (base CLIP is 20.38), so this measures the method, not the model's representation units.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed 32 randomly selected SAE mask latents and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.check: Random-ablation control of the TEVI mask; method analysis.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the bottom 32 SAE mask latents ranked by mask value and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.note: The relatively small drop contrasts with removing the top-ranked latents.
rows.check: Bottom-32 TEVI mask ablation; method analysis.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the top 64 SAE mask latents ranked by mask value and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.note: Strong loss after removing the top-ranked latents.
rows.check: Top-64 TEVI mask ablation; method analysis.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed 64 randomly selected SAE mask latents and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.check: Random-64 TEVI mask ablation; method analysis.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the bottom 64 SAE mask latents ranked by mask value and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.note: Bottom-latent ablation retains more retrieval performance than top-latent ablation.
rows.check: Bottom-64 TEVI mask ablation; method analysis.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the top 8 SAE mask latents ranked by grounding ρ and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.note: Grounding ρ is the correlation between a latent's mask value and the presence of its concept in the conditioning caption.
rows.check: ρ-ranked TEVI mask ablation; method analysis.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed 8 randomly selected SAE mask latents and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.check: Random-8 control for the ρ ranking; method analysis.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the bottom 8 SAE mask latents ranked by grounding ρ and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.
rows.note: The authors report that bottom-ranked ablations have less impact than top-ranked ablations.

rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the top 16 SAE mask latents ranked by grounding ρ and measured DOCCI image-to-text R@1.

rows.check: Random-32 control under the ρ ranking (15.2, distinct from r6's 15.58); method analysis.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CLIP ViT-B/16 on CC12M, with DOCCI captions and retrieval
reader_labels.reason: Some latents correlate with caption concepts and ranked latent removal affects retrieval, but only 20% of active latents pass the reported correlation threshold and the authors note imperfect SAE accuracy and comparable no-SAE retrieval in some setups (r1–r19).
